anomaly_def.Name: Optimizer Statistics Anomaly + Buffer Cache and Latch Contention Anomaly + Network and Connectivity Resource Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
Optimizer Statistics Anomaly : Optimizer input metadata is stale, incomplete, or misleading, causing systematic cardinality misestimates and sub-optimal execution-plan choices.
Buffer Cache and Latch Contention Anomaly : Hot buffer pages and the latching primitives that protect them become points of intense contention, forcing sessions to spin or block while reading or modifying shared pages.
Network and Connectivity Resource Anomaly : The transport and connection-handling layer cannot keep pace with the offered workload, leading to connection stalls, socket backlog growth, and packet-level retransmissions.

When these three root causes occur simultaneously, the database exhibits a multi-layered slowdown: misestimated plans drive access patterns that hammer a small set of pages, sharply increasing page-latch and buffer-busy waits; the resulting execution delays keep server backends busy and hold client sockets open longer, which in turn saturates listener queues and network bandwidth. Users observe erratic query latencies, timeouts during both execution and connection establishment, spikes in CPU spin time, swollen buffer-pool churn, ballooning active connection counts, and divergence between estimated and actual row counts in execution plans. Performance troubleshooting becomes difficult because symptoms manifest concurrently in optimizer statistics views, wait-class dashboards, and network/OS telemetry, each partially masking the others.

Causally, stale or missing statistics mislead the optimizer into choosing plans that repeatedly probe or modify a narrow set of pages (e.g., nested-loop joins on underestimated result sets or range scans on monotonic inserts), creating hot-page hotspots. The intensified latch contention elongates query runtime and keeps transactions open, inflating the number and lifetime of active connections. Prolonged sessions increase network socket occupancy and data-in-flight, pushing the listener, TCP buffers, or intermediary network devices toward saturation. Conversely, elevated network latency or connection throttling stretches transaction durations, raising concurrent access to already contended buffer pages and amplifying latch pressure. The feedback loop between poor plans, engine-level contention, and external connectivity bottlenecks can cascade into severe throughput collapse and widespread application timeouts.

entry.official_definition: The time limit for regular expression matching operations performed by the regular expression engine.
entry.trigger_condition: A regular expression match operation exceeds regexp_time_limit.
entry.workload_impact: The regular expression operation is constrained by the configured time limit.
entry.default_behavior: Defined as a MySQL server system variable.
entry.cause_analysis: This timeout is usually triggered when statement execution exceeds a configured execution-time budget because the operation runs too long or the workload is blocked behind other work.
entry.solution_guidance: Inspect query shape, access path quality, resource contention, and whether the timeout threshold should be reviewed together with the workload pattern.
